AccessBudgetWindow.description: One budget window as a platform reader sees it: usage is always visible. Three shapes: known (no unknown-cost request; remaining_microusd is a decimal), unknown (at least one unknown-cost request: every figure is present but remaining_microusd is null) and unavailable (the accounting row is unreadable: used_microusd, unresolved_usage, exhausted, settled_microusd, pending_held_microusd, unknown_held_microusd, unknown_cost_requests and remaining_microusd are all null together and headroom_status is unknown). A null group therefore implies headroom_status unknown, but unknown does not imply the null group (governance/totals.rs read_budget_report and BudgetReport::remaining, policies.rs budget_windows).

IdentityAdminCeilingNotification.description: Even Platform Admins never receive a personal workspace identity: personal=true forces workspace=null and a null/absent workspace_name. Non-personal references are Team/Project only.

IdentityAdminSummaryBudgetVisibility.description: Closed administrative projection: workspace-wide budgets visible.

IdentityCeilingDetails.description: Exact alerts::ceiling_conditions producer fields and wire types. workspace_name is nullable for personal events and omitted by non-Admin redaction; every other producer field is required. No workspace id, nested workspace or owner identity is permitted.

IdentityExportProfile.description: Profile of the signed-in person. Every export sits behind a verified browser session, and the only session writer (identity.rs callback) stores first/last_signed_in_at in the same statement, so both sign-in times are never null. disabled_at and platform_role stay NULLABLE: verify_session (identity.rs:1442) checks them in its own pool statement, and subject_export reads PROFILE (subject_export.rs:147) later in a separate snapshot after recording the audit event (:174-175), so a disable or role revocation in between is observable as a non-null disabled_at or a null platform_role. email is nulled only by account cleanup (lifecycle.rs), which subject_export PROFILE excludes.

anyOf.x-omg-unobserved-branch: The request is authenticated by verify_session (identity.rs:1442, a pool statement requiring users.disabled_at IS NULL) and the profile is read later in a separate snapshot (subject_export.rs:175 and :147), so only an administrator disabling the person in that window yields a timestamp; a test cannot interleave the two statements.

verify_session (identity.rs:1442) joins effective_platform_roles, but PROFILE (subject_export.rs:147) reads the role in a later snapshot, so a role revoked in that window yields null; a test cannot interleave the two statements.

details.description: Stored JSON incident payload, not a serde DTO. Fields vary by producer/kind; readers do not deserialize or close this map. Every *_microusd value is a non-null integer micro-USD string (unknown cost is reported in unknown_cost_requests, never as null). Each alerts.rs producer field is typed individually: pending_microusd is sum(held - held_unknown) read from budget_totals with no sign guard (migration 0015 has no >= 0 check), so drifted accounting can make it negative and it is signed; used_microusd (an incident needs used to reach a positive threshold of a positive reference), budget_microusd, spend_amount_microusd and min_spend_microusd (validated positive amounts), and current_microusd, baseline_total_microusd and baseline_hourly_microusd (settled ledger sums, CHECK(actual_microusd >= 0)) are unsigned. Any other *_microusd value from a producer not listed must still be an integer string (signed form). Admission-ceiling identity redaction is constrained by the separate variants below.

IdentityOwnAccessRequest.description: Requester-private projection: no requester_email or requester_display_name. The workspace name is the submitted snapshot, not its current discoverability/name.

IdentityRedactedCeilingNotification.description: Non-Admin projection of a non-personal event: no workspace identity/name, including nested details. IdentitySignedDecimal.description: Exact integer micro-USD that may be negative: governance totals::read returns settled+held with no non-negativity guard, so drifted accounting can report a negative string.

IdentityUnsignedDecimal.description: Exact nonnegative integer; money fields are micro-USD, never floating point.

IdentityWithdrawnAccessRequest.description: A withdrawn request. Always decided by the requester at the time of withdrawal and never linked to a membership grant: access_requests CHECKs (0066_access_requests.sql) require status='withdrawn' to carry decided_by=requester and a non-null decided_at, and only approved requests have an access_request_applications row. Requester-private projection: no requester_email or requester_display_name.

S6KnownBudgetWindow.description: A visible budget window whose accounting is exact: no request of the window has an unknown cost, so the remaining allowance is known (governance::totals BudgetReport::remaining). The report is valid only when unknown_cost_requests (unknown + unresolved - unresolved_unknown + unreserved executions) is 0 exactly when all three counters are 0 (read_budget_report's validity check, totals.rs:158-162), which fixes unresolved_usage to false and, because held_unknown_microusd must be 0 whenever unknown is 0, unknown_held_microusd to "0"; used_microusd is then settled plus pending held.

The first member is the canonical integer form; the second bounds it to a positive i64. The schema is stricter than the handler on one point: governance::money accepts leading zeros up to 19 characters ("007" is 7), which the canonical pattern refuses.

patch_api_v1_platform_oidc_group_mapping.description: Fields merged onto the stored mapping (an omitted field keeps its value, an explicit null clears platform_role, workspace_id or workspace_role) and then validated as a complete mapping. Cross-field rule, as far as the body decides it: when target_kind is present, platform requires a platform_role and null workspace_id and workspace_role, and workspace requires a workspace_id and workspace_role (admin or member) and a null platform_role, each for the fields the body names (directory.rs mapping_valid on the merged row). Without target_kind the stored row's kind decides, which the schema cannot see: a body that names only a workspace field for a platform mapping is accepted by the schema and refused by the handler. When target_kind is present, fields the body omits are still filled from the stored row: switching a platform mapping to workspace without also sending platform_role:null keeps the stored platform_role, so the schema accepts that body and the handler refuses it.

issuer.description: An https URL without credentials, query or fragment, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes (directory.rs mapping_valid counts bytes; x-omg-max-bytes states the byte limit and maxLength counts characters). The handler accepts what the WHATWG URL parser (reqwest::Url::parse) accepts with scheme https, a host, no user info, no query and no fragment. The schema pattern is a deliberately narrower subset: the literal form https://host[:port][/path], a host without whitespace, control characters or / ? # @ : [ ] % < > ^ | \, and a port of 0 to 65535 (an empty port is accepted, as by the parser). Remaining differences, each probed over HTTP: (1) the parser strips leading and trailing C0 controls and spaces (accepted by the schema too) and tab, CR and LF anywhere (inside the scheme or host the schema refuses them), and also accepts https:host, https:/host, https:///host and a backslash as the path separator (https://host\path), none of which the schema accepts; (2) the parser percent-decodes the host (a host containing %75 is read as u), which the schema refuses with its % exclusion, and refuses what IDNA or IPv4 parsing refuses (a numeric host outside the IPv4 range, a bracketed host that is not an IPv6 address), which the schema accepts because it checks characters only; (3) leading zeros beyond five port digits (https://host:000080) are accepted by the parser and refused by the schema; (4) the path admits any character but ? and # (the parser percent-encodes spaces, control characters and non-ASCII text in the path, and trims or strips surrounding whitespace and tab, CR and LF), so the schema accepts them there too; empty user info (https://@host) is accepted by the parser and the handler (the username is empty and there is no password) and refused by the schema's @ exclusion; (5) a development installation (GATEWAY_ENV=development) additionally accepts http on a loopback host, which the schema never does (the setting is process-wide, so it is probed only as a refusal outside development). The schema accepts only ASCII host names. The parser also accepts internationalized (non-ASCII) host names, each label of at most 1000 characters (idna uts46.rs refuses a longer one), which the schema refuses: a documented divergence pinned by HTTP probes (a 1000-character non-ASCII label and a short non-ASCII host with a long path are accepted by the handler and refused by the schema; a 1001-character label is refused by both). Non-ASCII text is accepted in the path, up to the 2048-byte limit.

info.description: INCOMPLETE contract skeleton (#81 PR1). Access extensions are minimum boundaries, not complete authority. Live owner, role, membership, personal-workspace and object-visibility checks remain authoritative. Personal details are owner-only; platform totals do not grant personal detail access. Shared members see their own activity unless an administrator or the object's visibility permits more; ownership checks can hide objects with 404. Auditor platform authority is read-only, independent User/membership entitlements remain usable. Credential families are exclusive, duplicate Authorization headers are refused, inference keys never authorize management, undeclared routes fail closed, and write scopes do not imply read scopes. BrowserAdminOnly includes Platform Admin even on GET. HEAD implicitly follows GET unless separately declared; no synthetic HEAD operations are listed. Request/response placeholders live in x-omg-request-schema and x-omg-response-schema until actual body presence, status and media types are reviewed; they are not permissive acceptance schemas.
